question: Under the RBI prudential norms for Urban Co-operative Banks, after how many days of interest or principal being in arrears is a bank prohibited from booking income on an accrual basis for any security?
answer: A bank is prohibited from booking income on an accrual basis in respect of any security if the interest or principal is in arrears for more than 90 days.
evidence: A bank shall not book income on accrual basis in respect of any security, irrespective of the category in which it is included, where the interest / principal is in arrears for more than 90 days.
source_text:
D. Booking of Income on Investments in Shares & Bonds

111. The investments are also subject to the prudential norms on income recognition. A bank shall not book income on accrual basis in respect of any security, irrespective of the category in which it is included, where the interest / principal is in arrears for more than 90 days.
doc_title: Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025 (Updated as on October 01, 2026)

question: Under RBI guidelines regarding Gold Loans, what instruments can authorized banks accept to extend gold metal loans to jewellery exporters who are customers of non-authorized banks?
answer: Authorized banks may extend gold metal loans to jewellery exporters who are customers of non-authorized banks by accepting a standby letter of credit or bank guarantee issued by the exporter's bankers, subject to the lending norms of the authorized bank and specified circular conditions.
evidence: In this connection we advise that the authorised banks may extend gold (metal) loans also to the jewellery exporters who are the customers of other non-authorized banks by accepting the stand by letter of credit or bank guarantee issued by their bankers
source_text:
Gold Loan against Bank Guarantee/Letter
of Credit issued by other banks

In terms of our circular No.DBOD.IBS.1519/23.67.001/98-99 dated 31st December 1998, authorized banks have been permitted to grant Gold (metal) loan as per Export Import Policy 1997-2002 and the Hand Book of Procedures of the Exim Policy subject to certain conditions mentioned in the circular.

2. In this connection we advise that the authorised banks may extend gold (metal) loans also to the jewellery exporters who are the customers of other non-authorized banks by accepting the stand by letter of credit or bank guarantee issued by their bankers, subject to authorised banks' own norms for lending and the conditions stipulated in our above mentioned circular.

Yours faithfully,

(Devaki Muthukrishnan)
General Manager

question: What immediate steps must a Credit Information Company (CIC) take upon experiencing a security breach and leakage of confidential customer-related information?
answer: When a breach of security and leakage of confidential customer-related information occurs, a Credit Information Company (CIC) must immediately notify the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Furthermore, the CIC is required to follow RBI's extant instructions regarding Incident Response and Recovery Management.
evidence: A CIC shall immediately notify RBI in the event of breach of security and leakage of confidential customer-related information. In these eventualities, the CIC shall adhere to the extant instructions issued by RBI from time to time on Incident Response and Recovery Management.
source_text:
26. A CIC shall review and monitor the security practices and control processes of its service providers on a regular basis and require the service provider to disclose security breaches.

27. A CIC shall immediately notify RBI in the event of breach of security and leakage of confidential customer-related information. In these eventualities, the CIC shall adhere to the extant instructions issued by RBI from time to time on Incident Response and Recovery Management.
